output.brief: The fall in first-contact resolution is mainly a billing-referral effect, not an agent or IVR problem. On 14 April, Finance's FC-0417 change cut in-call credit authority from £100 to £25 and automatically referred larger billing cases to the Billing Resolution team. Billing referrals jumped from 7% to 54% in that same week. Calls that were not referred kept their 82% FCR, and tenured agents fell by the same amount as the April intake, so the new starters are not the cause. The tariff rise and the IVR redesign do not fit the timing or the pattern. I am fairly confident in this, though the link from referrals to the site-wide drop rests on a dashboard that counts referred calls as unresolved, and complaints are only loosely tied to it. Next: do not put the April intake on performance plans. Run a limited trial of a higher in-call credit limit with post-call sampling on two teams, as Finance's controller suggested, and track FCR and unsupported credits. Pausing the IVR work is not justified by this evidence.
